title: GPT-6 Pro proves a quadratic-size threshold suffices for random permutations to contain every length-n pattern
summary: The paper proves that a uniformly random permutation of length 32n² contains every permutation of length n as a pattern with probability at least 1−exp(−c n/log n), for an absolute c>0 and sufficiently large n. This removes the prior log-log factor from the sufficient-length bound, resolves Alon’s open 1000n² problem, and establishes the correct Θ(n²) order.
organization: Yu Chen and Yiting Wang (affiliations not specified in arXiv record)

evidence.tested: The paper proves that a uniformly random permutation of length 32n² contains every permutation of length n as a pattern with probability at least 1−exp(−c n/log n), for an absolute c>0 and sufficiently large n.
evidence.unknown: ArXiv preprint. Authors report checking and digesting the proof; no separate independent validation is claimed here. The result is an asymptotic sufficient bound with constant 32 (the paper explains the constant can be reduced to any value greater than 1), not a sharp threshold constant.
evidence.ai_role: The authors state that GPT-6 Pro found the proof; they do not claim credit for its proof ideas, and say they verified and digested it and take responsibility for the manuscript.
